types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

cacheControl
directives.description:
Cache control directive for GraphQL fields and types

Examples:
- @cacheControl(maxAge: 3600) - Cache for 1 hour
- @cacheControl(maxAge: 0) - Don't cache (real-time data)
- @cacheControl(maxAge: 300, scope: PUBLIC) - Public cache for 5 minutes

args.name: inheritMaxAge
args.description: Whether to inherit max age from parent type

args.name: maxAge
args.description: Maximum age in seconds for cache TTL

args.name: scope

directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: oneOf
directives.description: Indicates exactly one field must be supplied and this field must not be `null`.

directives.name: ownerOnly
directives.description:
Require that the current user is the owner of the parent resource
Returns null for the field if user is not the owner (soft denial)
This is useful for sensitive fields that should only be visible to the owner

The owner check uses:
1. parent.userId (if exists) - compared to context.userId
2. parent.authorId (if exists) - for author-owned resources like recipes
3. parent.ownerId (if exists) - for explicitly owned resources

Example:
type User {
  email: String! @auth
  settings: UserSettings @ownerOnly
  notifications: [Notification!]! @ownerOnly
}

type Recipe {
  privateNotes: String @ownerOnly
}

directives.name: requireAccess
directives.description:
Require specific access level to a resource
Returns FORBIDDEN error if user doesn't have required access level

The resource ID is extracted from:
1. parent.id (for field resolvers)
2. args.id (for query/mutation arguments)

Access level mapping:
- OWNER role → OWNER, WRITE, READ access
- ADMIN/MEMBER roles → WRITE, READ access
- GUEST role → READ access

Example:
type ShoppingList {
  items: [Item!]! @requireAccess(resource: "ShoppingList", level: READ)
  collaborators: [Collaborator!]! @requireAccess(resource: "ShoppingList", level: OWNER)
}

type Mutation {
  deleteShoppingList(id: ID!): Boolean
    @requireAccess(resource: "ShoppingList", level: OWNER)
}

directives.name: requireRole
directives.description:
Require specific home membership role
Returns FORBIDDEN error if user doesn't have required role

Note: Uses existing MembershipRole enum (OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER, GUEST)

Example:
type Mutation {
  deleteHome(id: ID!): Boolean @requireRole(role: OWNER)
